Alpha 1.79.3 (town masonry, elemental landscapes and dungeon architecture)

  • Lanternhold buildings, courtyard walls and street furniture gain weathered masonry with quieter mortar and coordinated surface detail. Building placement, walking space and collisions remain unchanged.
  • Fire ground gains folded basalt and ash; Moonfrost gains softer weathered ice and rime, with beveled Tide Rib pier courses and attached tide marks. Stormcrown Reach gains wind-worn slate and gently billowed camp canvas. These are loading-time details, not per-frame cloth simulation.
  • Molten Core, Tempest Spire, Abyssal Well and Umbral Nexus gain coordinated color, relief and roughness and distinctive blind arcades, piers and trim. Blind arcades are decorative, not new passages. Existing wall bounds, floors, layouts, collision boxes, entrances and progression remain unchanged; transparent camera cutaway walls stay simple and readable. Verdant retains its established surfaces.
  • Elemental dungeon textures respect High/Low quality. Changing quality while inside an affected dungeon offers a reload instead of rebuilding the instance or resetting its progress. Existing texture counts remain unchanged; detailed walls and canvas add bounded geometry.
  • Desktop and phone-sized rendered checks cover equipped characters and the real HUD at ordinary gameplay zoom. This is a scoped visual patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze, full 1.87 art milestone, final modern-art approval, physical-phone party test or whole-game performance guarantee. Raised terrain remains disabled in production.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restriction, character animation, access, payment or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.2 (woodland rendering, Moonfrost surfaces and release trust)

  • Woodland crowns and ground cover use more selective render batches while retaining every tree, leaf and plant, their original detail and unchanged collisions. Static bounds reuse creation-time vertex work; no extra per-frame vertex scan. High woodland reference now measures 249,406 triangles and 338 draw calls within the original limits. All three High and Low reference views pass; this is not a whole-world or every-device performance guarantee.
  • Gloamwood leaves gain subtle veins and shadow-aware light wrapping. Rock materials use registered mineral detail across differently angled faces, and optional raised-world outcrops retain sharp cleaves with smoother weathered shoulders. Silhouettes and collision geometry stay unchanged.
  • Moonfrost ground gains weathered ice sheets, wind-deposited rime and short broken fissures with matching color, relief and roughness on High and Low. The existing texture count, geometry and gameplay stay unchanged.
  • The renderer respects saved graphics quality from startup; Low-quality startup no longer briefly creates High-quality postprocessing. Ground-anchored, snapped shadow coverage and conservative foliage shadow bounds preserve off-screen shadows, restoring temporary flags after normal rendering, errors and disposal.
  • Deployment uses a pinned public host key, strict verification and bounded SSH waits. Native QA runs only from trusted production branches and the canonical repository; ordinary hosted checks retain separate queues. This does not repair external SSH routing or bypass deployment guards.
  • This is a scoped rendering/release-trust patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze or the full 1.87 art milestone. Raised-Earth live integration, final modern-art/equipped-party review, human pacing and supported-device acceptance remain open.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restriction, animation, access, payment or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.1 (realm-ground polish and stricter browser origins)

  • Gloamwood ground gains clearer soil and moss layering, warmer fallen leaves and coordinated shallow relief and roughness. Registered fields stay in place across High and Low quality; no additional textures or draw calls, terrain displacement or collision changes.
  • Stormcrown's ground gains broken wind-worn slate layers and pale scree deposits, with matching color, shallow relief and roughness on High and Low. Existing terrain textures and geometry stay the same; the added geological fields are generated during loading, not each frame.
  • Browser WebSocket admission rejects malformed Origin URLs, invalid ports, blank or duplicate Origin headers. Existing trusted domains and local development ports remain; native clients without an Origin still require normal authentication.
  • Failed equipment-model binding releases partially prepared owned parts without changing cached assets or previously equipped gear and body coverage. Older failed loading requests cannot clear a newer equipment request's visual status; successful item fit and animations remain unchanged.
  • Deployment checks free space on the checkout and actual Docker storage filesystems before cleanup, image builds or service replacement. The default 2 GiB minimum refuses low or unknown storage without automatic deletion; it is not a guarantee of peak build or backup capacity.
  • This is a scoped polish/security patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze. Raised-Earth production delivery, the remaining High woodland performance limit and final modern-art review remain open; the unfinished future terrain/performance branch is not included.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restrictions, animation, access or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.0 (multiplayer performance and lighter equipped characters)

  • Living unstuck requests no longer instantly refill health. Like Recall, they preserve both resource bars and use normal 10%-per-second town recovery; death respawns still restore health and mana. Cooldowns, gear and Well Rested remain intact.
  • Enemy targeting and nearby-player lookup reuse bounded live snapshots and a spatial player index. Simulation and replication share coherent current-frame data instead of repeatedly rebuilding player lists or copying character inventories. Player visibility, threat, attack ranges, party credit and authoritative combat rules remain unchanged.
  • Snapshot caches are prepared before recipient workers, use actor identity to avoid repeatedly hashing IDs, and lock only the individual actor being encoded; owner-only character data is never shared with observers. Same-cell movement avoids unnecessary spatial membership locks, while crossing a cell boundary still updates both indexes together. These changes do not omit actors or reduce simulation frequency.
  • Equipped class models now share identical skeleton data only within one character or one equipment generation. Cached source assets, other players and body/equipment ownership stay independent; joint order and inverse matrices must match exactly. Geometry, textures, morphs, item fit and animations retain their original quality.
  • Casino floor cutaways skip hidden rig work. Sitting updates only necessary ancestor transforms before publishing the complete pose, avoiding redundant whole-character traversal. Both floors pass the original controlled High/Low frame-time targets with 40 fully equipped authored characters, 20 visible per floor; this is not a promise for every device or network scene.
  • Water, Fire and Air foliage now use conservative spatial draw bounds like Gloamwood. Off-screen instances can be culled without removing trees, changing their appearance or altering collisions; all four realm image/shadow comparisons pass.
  • Brief login bursts can wait up to 250 ms for an existing credential worker, with at most 16 waiting requests. Password-check concurrency and per-account limits do not increase; overload still fails safely. Connections closed or replaced while waiting cannot continue authentication or receive delayed replies.
  • Casino presence and readiness reuse a request-local current-player roster instead of repeatedly scanning every monster and fence. Live seat ownership, readiness revisions, reconnect reservations and scene cleanup remain unchanged; no roster is cached between requests.
  • Poker buy-ins distinguish a changed hand from an invalid stake, so players get clearer table feedback. Test clients react promptly to fresh betting offers without repeating uncertain wagers or counting unobserved payouts; game timers and betting limits remain unchanged.
  • Representative testing covers 100 simultaneous clients on one server: combat parties, paid casino play, social activity, town, an Earth raid with earned boss-checkpoint returns and repair waves, and a naturally scheduled Root event. The current integrated trial passed all 100 independent save checks and gameplay gates, with 112.96 seconds of common activity. Measured update and broadcast phase means totaled 18.85 ms against the original 33 ms target, without relaxing the workload or deadlines. All four event participants completed every wave and all five raid participants finished the assault and crystal repair. Failed experiments remain recorded; this controlled, shared-host test is not 100-player capacity certification or launch signoff.
  • Card-table ordering rejects stale state; blackjack distinguishes a changed round from an invalid stake without retrying a wager. Bounded save/shutdown coverage preserves normal progress and wallet ownership. No account wipe, new schema migration, currency conversion, reward change or beta-access restriction. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.78.0 (service diagnostics and independent outage alerts)

  • Administration now includes an explicitly refreshed Service diagnostics view: readiness, release, memory, broadcast queues, character-save/recovery and Gold/EP transfer counts, plus separate simulation and broadcast timings. Eighteen fixed rows retain unavailable measurements rather than inventing zeros; durable role checks and audited reads remain required.
  • A separate opt-in monitor detects sustained outages and recovery even if the game process stops. The owner approved existing admin email recipients and current hosting/Postmark: 30-second probes, three failures before an alert, two healthy probes before recovery, and outage reminders no more than every 30 minutes. Email attempts have a shared one-minute minimum interval, finite timeout, no ambiguous retries and no tracking.
  • The independent Docker service validates its exact configuration without network or email requests before deployment, restarts unless explicitly stopped, and writes sanitized incident records to the existing host journal. Healthy polling is silent. Journal retention follows existing host policy; this does not guarantee time-based retention or off-machine coverage during a complete host/network outage.
  • Optional latency, memory, queue, active-call and local storage budgets stay disabled until measured and explicitly configured. Process counters reset on restart and include retries/rejections; they are not balances, unique payouts, financial compensation or 100-player capacity certification. Tokens, recipients, raw errors and player records never appear in the diagnostics or incident output.
  • The single owner-approved Postmark test was accepted and its inbox receipt confirmed; ongoing notification readiness is verified separately. No account wipe, schema migration, currency/reward rule, player audit retention or provider retention change. Full prior patch history remains below; the remaining roadmap and launch qualification are not declared complete.

Alpha 1.77.0 (safer hosting and verified proxy contracts)

  • Fresh custom-host TLS setup validates hostnames and ports before privileged work. It refuses existing configuration files, directories and even dangling links instead of replacing a working site. Missing Certbot is refused before bootstrap writes.
  • The installer rejects play.eidolonrealms.com and server.eidolonrealms.com, including case and trailing-dot variants: these require the additive two-host configuration, keeping the frontend on Pages and the game API on its own proxy.
  • Certificate requests and renewal dry-runs are scoped to the selected certificate. Existing installations use inspection and a named dry-run, not a reinstall. The owner verified a successful renewal simulation for both game domains on October 6. A successful timer alone is not proof that a future renewal challenge will succeed.
  • A native isolated Nginx regression checks exact backend paths, release queries, forwarding headers, production WebSocket Origin rules, binary frames and clean disconnects. It never loads installed configuration or changes a system service.
  • Operator guidance separates staging projects, loopback ports, credentials, Mongo volumes and private journals. A separate Git worktree is not a separate running environment. Restart policies and manual-stop/reboot limitations are explicit.
  • Public IPv4 is verified; public IPv6 and long idle sessions remain unverified. Outbound Pages DNS settings do not force players onto IPv4. DNS remains unchanged, and dual-stack launch support is not claimed.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, retention change, balance change or payment feature. Existing characters, Gold, EP and private activity journals remain intact. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.76.0 (lighter saves and reliable recovery at scale)

  • Login and character recovery fetch the selected save instead of unrelated characters and account metadata. Original first-character selection, account identity, equipment, progression and reconnect protections are preserved.
  • Live updates read a lightweight position, scene and Resonance view without repeatedly copying bags, stash contents and saved receipts. Full character saves remain intact; dungeon room tracking and owner-only progress stay synchronized.
  • Save journals use per-account lock shards so one stalled account does not hold up unrelated shards. Each account's writes, confirmations and ownership checks remain serialized.
  • New ground-item deliveries and casino wallet effects keep compact durable checkpoints instead of growing a receipt entry for every new action. Existing receipts, earned items, Gold and EP remain preserved; retries and restarts do not duplicate rewards or wagers.
  • The Trading House and slot machines recover saved work in small startup batches. Invalid or incomplete recovery keeps the affected service unavailable rather than exposing partially recovered decisions. Outstanding claims, refunds and funded payouts are retained.
  • Schema24 adds ordered ground-delivery uniqueness and Schema25 marks casino wallet checkpoints. Upgrade preserves account data and backups; older writers refuse the newer schema, so changing only the server image is not a safe downgrade. No account wipe, receipt pruning, retention change, balance or payout-rule change.
  • Historical receipts can still grow; these measured persistence improvements are not 100-player capacity certification. Later operations, hosting, recovery and beta gates remain separate. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.75.0 (private account support and reviewed data exports)

  • Account help before world entry and the in-game report form accept Account Data Export and Account Removal Request cases. Privacy requests attach no automatic diagnostics. Check your own saved reference for review status; case resolution does not mean data was delivered or removed.
  • Administrators review private cases and separately confirm reversible owner-export approval. Approved owners open fresh private account support, sign in, check their request and provide their current password to prepare a section. Save section locally is a separate click; paging is manual and every page requires fresh proof. Closing or disconnecting discards prepared files and passwords.
  • Nineteen bounded owner-facing sections cover profile, character gameplay, submitted reports, retained sessions, social relationships, marketplace, guilds, competitive and raid records, and applicable trade, reward, item, administration and casino records. Every file explains its coverage and omissions: this is not a complete account archive or restore image. Other players' private data, credentials, hidden casino decks and staff-only notes are excluded.
  • Data-handling notices appear before login, in Settings and account support. Removal remains an administrator-reviewed request, not an enabled erasure action. Read-only dependency review cannot authorize deletion. No automatic deletion or retention changes; provider and device copies require separate handling.
  • Character saves and reconnects are bound to the original account identity, preventing a replacement account with the same name from inheriting an old live session or pending save. Schema23 adds a writer-compatibility marker, not an account wipe. Upgrade preserves a consistent backup, rejects unresolved legacy journals before migration and restarts the unchanged old server on that refusal. A schema22 server cannot write schema23.
  • The private account-download page suppresses game analytics loading; custom analytics forward only coarse allowlisted fields and safe page context. Existing provider settings remain unchanged, and browser extensions, earlier collection and external provider retention are outside that page's protection. Recovery messages explicitly disable open/link tracking.
  • Queued reconnects report revoked tokens as invalid or expired without consuming replacement tokens. Test tooling removes the vulnerable sprintf-js dependency while retaining Jest30 and verified YAML configuration support.
  • No payment feature, reward or balance change. Later 1.76–1.99 work, real-player progression validation and 100-player capacity remain separate gates. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.74.7 (town service layout, faster jumps and durable activity)

  • The stash sits between the quest-giver smithy and Oathfire Forge, facing east with its neighbors. The western planter moves out of the service approach, and smithy collision follows its walls rather than roof and sign overhangs.
  • Long click-to-jump flights arrive within three seconds; short hops stay quick. Client prediction matches the server, and live flights use elapsed time so delayed simulation frames cannot stretch their duration. Existing landing constraints, airborne input guards and casino walking-only rules remain.
  • Admin activity history remains in persistent MongoDB storage. Deployment cleanup explicitly preserves logs and pending activity journals, whose path is pinned to the persistent volume. Existing 90-day default retention is unchanged; updates do not reset history or backfill missing older session durations.
  • No account wipe, schema migration or payment feature. This maintenance does not complete unfinished 1.75–1.79 milestones or certify 100-player capacity. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.74.6 (persistent casino table timelines)

  • Blackjack, Hold'em, roulette and baccarat keep the newer ready table view when an older lobby or previous hand arrives late. Ordering now follows the table's persistent version across hand transitions, not just the current hand's revision.
  • Shared seats and occupants still refresh. Changed ownership, tables, currencies, unavailable or saving feedback, and equal or newer views retain their normal behavior. Exact decimal-string versions avoid rounding large counters.
  • Wager authority, payouts, timers and currencies are unchanged. No account wipe, schema migration, access change or payment feature is included. Earlier connection, loot, real-player administration and selling fixes remain included.
  • This targeted correction does not certify 100-player capacity or complete unfinished 1.75–1.79 milestones. Full prior patch history remains below.
